newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian state to ban lesbians from donor sperm.
newsitem.headline: Australian state to ban lesbians from donor sperm.

text.p: An Australian state health minister said on Monday he would bring in a law banning lesbians from using fertility clinics despite an anti-discrimination tribunal granting a gay woman access to donor sperm.

Queensland Health Minister Mike Horan said he would amend laws to close a "lifestyle loophole" and ensure fertility clinics were used only by the "traditional family" of a man and woman who have trouble reproducing due to medical problems.

"They (fertility clinics) weren't established to suit a particular lifestyle. They were established to provide assistance...to people who had reproductive problems," Horan told Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio.
"It's time in society that we started to take a stance about what are our standards of family," said Horan, adding he would introduce a law banning lesbians from fertility clinics.
Horan's comments follow an anti-discrimination tribunal ruling last Friday allowing a lesbian access to donor sperm to have a child.

The 23-year-old unidentified woman sued a Queensland fertility clinic for refusing her access to donor sperm, claiming it caused humiliation and depression. The tribunal awarded the woman A$7,500 (US$5,700).
Only two of Australia's six states, Queensland and New South Wales, have no regulations governing in-vitro fertilisation programmes and sperm banks.
In the state of Victoria, Australia's second most populous state, access to sperm banks is restricted to legally married couples who have been unable to conceive for 12 months.
